categories.main_business_segments: TechnipFMC operates through two primary business segments: Subsea and Surface Technologies. The Subsea segment provides integrated design, engineering, procurement, manufacturing, installation, and life-of-field services for subsea systems and infrastructure used in offshore oil and gas production. The Surface Technologies segment designs, manufactures, and services products and systems for conventional and unconventional land and shallow water oil and gas exploration and production, as well as emerging energy transition applications such as carbon storage and hydrogen.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Core technologies include proprietary subsea production systems (SPS), umbilicals, risers, flowlines (SURF), subsea robotics (Schilling Robotics), and digital platforms like Subsea Studio™. The company leverages integrated engineering, procurement, construction, and installation (iEPCI™) models, configure-to-order (CTO) manufacturing (Subsea 2.0®), and advanced digital and automation solutions for both subsea and surface operations. Surface Technologies utilizes modular, digital, and automation-enabled systems for wellheads, pressure pumping, and flow management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: TechnipFMC's main customers are major integrated oil companies, national oil companies, and independent exploration and production companies. The Subsea segment serves offshore oil and gas operators, while Surface Technologies caters to both onshore and offshore operators, including those involved in carbon capture, hydrogen, and geothermal projects. The company is increasingly targeting customers in the energy transition space, such as those developing carbon storage and offshore renewables.
categories.geographic_coverage: TechnipFMC operates globally, with significant presence in the Americas (notably the United States and Brazil), Europe (UK, Norway, France, Netherlands), Africa (Angola, Nigeria, Ghana), the Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar), and Asia-Pacific (India, Malaysia, Australia, Indonesia). The majority of revenue is generated outside the United States, with strong positions in deepwater offshore basins and growing activity in the Middle East and Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily as an equipment and solutions provider at the midstream and downstream points of the oil and gas supply chain, delivering integrated systems and services for production, processing, and transportation. In the energy transition, TechnipFMC is positioning itself as a system architect and integrator for carbon storage, hydrogen, and offshore renewables, leveraging its expertise across the value chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: TechnipFMC's strategic focus is on technology innovation, digital transformation, and industrialization of its product offerings. Key R&D initiatives include the Subsea 2.0® CTO platform, all-electric subsea systems, hybrid-flexible pipe technologies, digital twins, and automation. The company is also investing in new energy solutions for carbon capture and storage, offshore floating renewables, and hydrogen, aiming to enable clients' energy transition and decarbonization goals.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of engineered products, integrated project execution (iEPCI™), services, and leasing of equipment and vessels. The company also earns revenue from aftermarket services, digital solutions, and, increasingly, from new energy projects. Contracts are often long-term and may include fixed-price, time-and-materials, and performance-based components.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: TechnipFMC is positioned as the only fully integrated provider capable of delivering the complete suite of subsea FEED, SPS, SURF, installation, and life-of-field services. Key competitors include Baker Hughes, SLB (Schlumberger), Halliburton, Subsea 7, McDermott, NOV, Oceaneering, Cactus Wellhead, and OneSubsea. The company differentiates itself through its integrated commercial model, technology leadership, and digital innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, TechnipFMC reported $9.1 billion in revenue, up 16% year-over-year, with a backlog of $14.4 billion and operating cash flow of $961 million. Subsea accounted for $7.8 billion in revenue, while Surface Technologies contributed $1.3 billion. The company has demonstrated strong growth in subsea orders and profitability, with a positive outlook supported by a robust project pipeline and investment-grade credit ratings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: TechnipFMC emphasizes its ability to deliver fully integrated, technologically advanced, and digitally enabled solutions that improve project economics, accelerate time to first production, and reduce carbon intensity. Its unique iEPCI™ model, Subsea 2.0® CTO platform, and digital offerings provide clients with cost savings, operational efficiency, and sustainability advantages, positioning the company as a key enabler of both traditional and new energy developments.
